match.reason: The bank point is a Year 12 NSW card on what liveability is and how it is measured across several measures, while the new point is about how a liveable place meets the needs of specific groups such as young people, older people and people with disability, so it teaches a different idea at a different depth.

note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Question a, other: Why (a) says liveability is 'not what it costs'. This clashes with point 4, where cost is a criterion for judging a strategy. The distractor is wrong because stairs-only entrances keep people out (and stairs do not generally cost more than ramps and lifts), not because cost never matters.

rejected.title: Liveability for everyone
card: A place is liveable when it works well for the different people who live there. People of different ages and abilities can have different needs.
Young people
Teenagers need safe places to meet, play sport and spend time, such as a skate park or a youth space.
Older people
Many older people need seats to rest on, paths that are easy to walk without steep steps, and transport that is easy to reach.
People with disability
Ramps, wide doorways and lifts let people who use wheelchairs or prams get in and move around. Buses and trains that are easy to board help too.
rejected.remember: A place is more liveable when it meets the needs of people of all ages and abilities.

a.q: Why does a town with a new library that has only stairs at its entrance fall short on liveability?
opts: Some people cannot get in, so it does not work for everyone
Libraries are not a service that adds to liveability
Only older people use libraries, so teenagers miss out
Stairs cost more to build than ramps and lifts
a.why: A liveable place works for people of different ages and abilities. Stairs can keep out people who use wheelchairs or prams, and many older people who find steps hard. The option about building costs is wrong, because liveability is about who a place works for, not what it costs.
a.clue: Think about who could not use the entrance.

b.q: Tom's town has many parks for small children but nowhere for teenagers to meet or play sport. What would make the town work better for everyone?
opts: Build a skate park or youth space for teenagers
Add more play equipment for small children
Build wider roads for cars through the town
Move the parks further from the town centre
b.why: Teenagers have different needs from small children, so a place for them makes the town work for more people. More child play equipment helps the group that is already served.
